cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Them Keep Hope
cards.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep the seed packets. The allotment letter says we're on the waiting list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've covered our number. If it's another year indoors, I'm giving up gardening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. The important bit is we're on it. Let's start tomatoes on my windowsill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll get tired of them before we get a plot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my sunny room. I'll move the bed; keep the packets.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders packet retention, A3 selects only the hopeful part of the letter and A5 grants own room/moves bed, using control over information and space to keep B gardening.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 covered-number challenge and giving-up threat cause A3 windowsill plan; B4 doubts its durability, causing A5 a larger concrete space commitment.

relationship.evidence: B2 sees the hidden detail and B4 worries about exhausting A hospitality, plausible reasons the hopeful workaround may fail.

heightening.evidence: B4 host-fatigue concern causes A5 to surrender the sunny room and move bed, making hope materially supportable.

specificity.evidence: A1 allotment waiting list and B2 concealed rank establish information; seeds/windowsill/room keep the activity concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 moving the bed so packets survive earns a disproportionate protective concession from B4, with specific care.
